params._roi_note: ROI centred on beam at coarse bias 2/2 (fine 1.5/2.15): probe-verified 2026-07-21, full-sensor CoM (x 919, y 507). Re-derive via contrib/probe_frame.json only on an alignment change.

pipeline._comment: frame -> UDP viewer, so you can watch the beam + tracking (same as steering_fsp)

params._note: tracked 20x20 window, threshold 22 -- matches conf_bode_y.json exactly so the parport sweep measures the same sensor the piplate sweep did.

pipeline._comment: CoM -> UDP viewer so the tracked centroid can be overlaid on the frame
Replace the y/tip element (0) with the swept sine; read CoM y as response

params._tuning: v2 (2026-07-17): 60 log points x 49 cycles, 7 integer-cycle segments per point for per-point error bars + coherence quality (<0.9 flagged). Integer-cycle segment boundaries remove the partial-cycle DC/line leakage of the old fixed-time cutoff. freq_start 5 Hz (was 1): the flat+delay plant is fully pinned by the 5-30 Hz K band and 49 cycles at 1 Hz would cost ~50 s/point.
params._amplitude: scale is 1.0 V/unit and offset 2.5 V, so amplitude IS the drive in volts: 0.1 sweeps 2.4..2.6 V, i.e. 2.5 V +/- 100 mV, matching the x sweep.
params._amplitude2: half-amplitude (+/-50 mV, i.e. 2.45..2.55 V) linearity/dead-zone check; bode_plot flags a >10% |H| change between amplitudes. y is the axis that previously sat near the FSM stiction/dead-zone at low drive -- if mag2 comes back < mag by ~15% and NONLINEAR is flagged, raise both amplitudes rather than trusting Ky. The converter is NOT a candidate cause: ~2600 codes at 76 uV/LSB, sitting at mid-range.
params._avoid_freqs: nudge sweep points off the measured bench lines (a line inside the lock-in skirt biases the point coherently -- segments do not average it out).
params.config: y/tip open-loop plant through the PARPORT DAC (DAC81404, spi link, mmio, range 0-5 V on a +/-12 V supply), no coarse stage, ch0=y / ch1=x. Drive 2.5 V +/- 100 mV, i.e. 2.4..2.6 V (scale 1.0 V/unit, offset 2.5, amplitude 0.1). 32x32 exp250 gain100 bw100, beam-centred ROI via start_x/start_y, tracked 20x20 thr22. Purpose: derive BOTH Ky and tau for this transport from scratch. tau: expect SHORTER than the piplate-era 5.6 fr. Ky: expect WELL BELOW the old 0.66 -- the fine channel is divided downstream and scale is halved (1.0 vs 2.0 V/unit), so the old value is an upper bound, not a prediction. K uses <=30 Hz, tau uses the full 5-300 Hz slope.
params._start_delay: hold injection at 0 (= the channel parked at 0 V) for 30 s before the sweep starts. No coarse stage to settle any more, but the hold gives the FSM and camera AGC a quiet, known starting point and lets bode_plot measure its baseline.
params._output_file: distinct filename on purpose: do NOT overwrite the piplate-era fsm_bodey_722_full4.pdf.

pipeline._note: PARPORT DAC. TWO channels only -- there is no coarse stage: ch0 = y/tip (DACA), ch1 = x/tilt (DACB). Here y is driven and x is parked (scale 0).
pipeline._range: 0-5 (unipolar, DACRANGE code 0x0), biased at mid-range 2.5 V so the command has 2.5 V of headroom both ways without a bipolar range. 76 uV/LSB -- 2x finer than +-5, since all 16 bits now cover 5 V instead of 10.
pipeline._avss_note: GROUND AVSS for this unipolar range (EVM J17 pin 5). SLASEH2A 7.5 specifies the unipolar accuracy figures at AVSS = 0 V; the -21.5 V <= AVSS < 0 conditions are the bipolar ones. Negative AVSS with a unipolar range is legal per 7.3 but uncharacterized, and doubles analog dissipation. The 1.25-1.5 V footroom that would argue for it is conditioned on +-10/+-15 mA of load current -- unloaded, zero code sits ~7.5 mV off ground. See conf_bode_par_x.json for the full reasoning.
pipeline._scale_sign: y keeps the POSITIVE sign the piplate config used (was +2, now +1.0), and x keeps its negative sign in the steering configs. The sign is a property of the optical/mechanical path, not the converter, so it carries over even though the magnitude does not.

params._no_range_max: auto-ranging deliberately NOT enabled for a sweep: a mid-sweep range change would glitch the output for a frame and step the quantization, both of which land in the lock-in as a bogus point. The sweep never leaves 100..300 mV anyway.
params._verify: off in a swept/timed run: verify turns each write into 3 frames plus a non-posted status read per bit.
params._sync_update: left off: only one channel is driven in this sweep, so there is no inter-channel skew to remove.
